cohort: 71 preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation, admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit at King Abdulaziz University Hospital between January and December 2019.
finding: 27% of preterm infants developed hyponatremia, with lower gestational age, lower birth weight, exclusive breastfeeding, long-term TPN, and prescribed diuretics and antibiotics identified as significant risk factors for late-onset hyponatremia, which was associated with longer hospital stays, extra-uterine growth retardation, CLD, and sepsis.
mod_finding: None of the investigated maternal characteristics, including method of delivery, were significantly associated with hyponatremia.
